theSharpestTest_canIntegerGuardScanBeEva.question: v4's LB-C2-01 repair is class-based: integer_guard_scan walks the checker's own AST on every run and refuses any bare numeric comparison against a wire-sourced value. That is the identical pattern an independent reviewer just defeated in check-evidence-v10.py (EV10-IR-01). Can it be evaded here?
theSharpestTest_canIntegerGuardScanBeEva.answer: YES. integer_guard_scan is evadable by the same class of indirection that defeated _collect_path_calls in check-evidence-v10.py. I demonstrated this constructively, not by argument. HOWEVER — and this is the whole of the grading — no evasion is reachable on the frozen bytes, and no evasion produces a green run, because an INDEPENDENT NON-AST layer catches every one of them. The finding is therefore MAJOR and NON-BLOCKING, and I establish the non-reachability by AST-level enumeration of references rather than by assumption.

howTheScanModelsTheWorld.functionUniverse: _module_functions() takes ONLY ast.FunctionDef nodes in tree.body. Top-level async functions, all class methods, all nested functions and all lambdas are outside the universe.
howTheScanModelsTheWorld.reachability: _reachable() follows ONLY ast.Call whose .func is an ast.Name literally present in that universe. This is precisely the EV10-IR-01 shape.
howTheScanModelsTheWorld.taint: _tainted_names() seeds from a function's positional and kw-only args, then propagates ONLY through single-target ast.Assign whose value is a Subscript, a .get() call, or an already-tainted Name.
howTheScanModelsTheWorld.numericModel: _numeric_literal() accepts ONLY a bare ast.Constant int/float.
howTheScanModelsTheWorld.operators: ast.Is, ast.IsNot, ast.In and ast.NotIn are skipped outright.

whyThisIsNotBlocking_establishedByEnumer.rule: The finding is only non-blocking if NO false accept is reachable on the frozen bytes. I established that by enumerating references at the AST level, as required, and separately by an exhaustive behavioural sweep.
whyThisIsNotBlocking_establishedByEnumer.enumeration1_callShapes: Across the whole 3238-line module there are 1548 call sites: 733 with an ast.Name callee and 815 with an ast.Attribute callee. There are ZERO call sites whose callee is neither — no Subscript-callee dispatch, no Call-callee (getattr(...)(...)) dispatch, no Starred dispatch.
whyThisIsNotBlocking_establishedByEnumer.enumeration2_indirectionPrimitives: ZERO uses of getattr/eval/exec/globals/vars/locals/__import__ for function dispatch. The only exec/compile pairs are the two verified-snapshot loaders. ZERO decorators on any top-level function. ZERO top-level AsyncFunctionDef. The only 6 top-level classes are AuthorityLoadError, PinMismatch, UnsupportedInvocation, _VerifiedSourceLoader, Authority and _TupleToSet — infrastructure, carrying 7 methods total, none of which validates wire data.
whyThisIsNotBlocking_establishedByEnumer.enumeration3_dispatchTables: Three genuine function-reference dispatch tables exist — CONTRACT_MUTATIONS (line 2788), SOURCE_MUTATIONS (line 2935) and SCAN_MUTATIONS (line 2973). All three hold only _m_* / _s_* MUTATION AUTHORS, which mutate a fixture and never validate wire data. None is in the validator closure and none contains any numeric comparison.
whyThisIsNotBlocking_establishedByEnumer.enumeration4_myOwnWiderScan: I wrote my own integer-guard scan widened on five independent axes: it scans all 154 function-like nodes rather than 143 top-level FunctionDefs; its reachability follows Name calls, Attribute calls, bare function references, dispatch-table membership and lambda bodies; its taint model additionally covers walrus, AnnAssign, AugAssign, tuple/list unpack, for-targets, comprehension targets, with-targets, nested-function and lambda parameters, and .pop()/.setdefault()/next()/getattr() results, to a fixpoint; its numeric model additionally accepts module-level names bound to numeric constants; and it does not skip In/NotIn. On the frozen bytes it finds ZERO unguarded sites — 0 against literal constants and 0 against named constants or numeric containers.
whyThisIsNotBlocking_establishedByEnumer.enumeration5_exhaustiveTextualSweep: Independently of any reachability model, I swept EVERY ast.Compare in the entire module for a numeric-literal operand. There are exactly SEVEN in 3238 lines, and every one compares a Python-internal integer, never wire data: _is_semver len(...)<=96; _tainted_names len(node.targets)==1; selftest_reachability_scan sum(...)==1; run_source_mutations broken>0 and clean==0; selftest len(base_findings)>10; _parse_argv len(positional)>1. There is no eighth site, guarded or unguarded, anywhere in the file.
whyThisIsNotBlocking_establishedByEnumer.conclusion: The scan's WEAKNESS IS REAL AND STRUCTURAL, but its BLIND SPOT IS CURRENTLY EMPTY. No unguarded numeric comparison against wire data exists anywhere in the frozen bytes, by any reachability model including one much wider than the author's, and no false accept is reachable.

aLiveDemonstrationThatTheBlindSpotIsNotH.finding: The author's reachability model ALREADY MISSES a real, shipped, wire-data validator. _is_relative_path (line 472) validates caller-supplied requestedPaths strings. Its ONLY reference in the entire module is as a CALLBACK — `validator=_is_relative_path` at line 713 — never as an ast.Call with a Name callee. It is therefore absent from the author's reached set of 69 functions but present in my reached set of 77.
aLiveDemonstrationThatTheBlindSpotIsNotH.exposure: NONE TODAY. _is_relative_path is correctly written: it routes its one numeric test through int_in_range(len(...), 1, 4096). So the miss costs nothing on these bytes.
aLiveDemonstrationThatTheBlindSpotIsNotH.significance: It converts the finding from 'a hypothetical evasion an attacker could construct' into 'the model demonstrably fails to cover a function the authors themselves already wrote and shipped'. The next such callback may not be written correctly, and the scan would not say so.

LB-C2-01.priorDefect: v3 guarded both commitment-bearing schemaVersion fields with a bare inequality against integer 1. True == 1 and 1.0 == 1 in the host language, so JSON true was ADMITTED and committed to a SECOND digest, and JSON 1.0 was ADMITTED and then raised an unguarded ValueError inside the canonical encoder.
myVerificationNotAReplay: I drove all 10 type-distinct spellings (integer 1, true, false, 1.0, '1', 2, 0, null, [1], {}) at BOTH commitment-bearing positions across ALL SEVEN valid PlanIntent fixtures. ZERO deviations: integer 1 is the only admitted spelling, every other spelling produces a typed C2I-02 finding naming the observed JSON type, and every admitted case also ENCODES — zero admit-then-raise.

Site 3, planIdentityInputs.planSchemaMajor, which the author says the sweep found and the finding did not name by location: CONFIRMED PRESENT AND REPAIRED. Integer 1 admits; true, false, 1.0, '1', 2, 0, null, [1] and {} are all rejected with C2I-06.
Site 4, Coverage.schemaVersion: CONFIRMED. Integer 1 admits; the other nine spellings produce a typed C2X naming the JSON type.

Site 5, planIntentTotalityMatrix.caseCount, the second site the author says the sweep found: CONFIRMED PRESENT. Every one of the ten spellings produces findings; this is a contract-authoring self-consistency field rather than a wire field, which is why it is guarded but not caller-reachable.

I THEN WENT FURTHER, as required, and swept for ANY remaining bare numeric comparison against a JSON-sourced value anywhere in the module — not merely in the author's reachable closure. Result: exactly seven numeric comparisons exist in 3238 lines and all seven compare Python-internal integers (see theSharpestTest.enumeration5). There is no sixth site, named or unnamed.
LB-C2-01.coordinatorClaimReproduced: Confirmed independently: True, 1.0 and '1' are now rejected; integer 1 admits; integer 2 rejects.
LB-C2-01.residualOnTheRepairMechanism: The VALUE-level repair is complete and correct. The CLASS-level repair — the AST scan — is evadable; see finding IR-C2V4-01. That does not reopen LB-C2-01, because the exact-type guards themselves are correct at every site and the behavioural census independently enforces the property.

LB-C2-02.priorDefect: validate_coverage raised on hostile roots and silently conformed six FALSY relation values because it wrote `if factplane and relation:`, skipping the declared C2X registry lookup. 58 of 81 mutations produced no finding.
myVerificationNotAReplay: 8 hostile Coverage roots (null, integer, boolean, float, string, empty array, non-empty array, empty object): 8/8 return a named C2X-ROOT finding. Critically, they return it through the UNGUARDED _validate_coverage as well — zero raises — so the repair is a real non-object-root guard, not merely a try/except wrapper that converts a traceback into a generic message.

6 falsy relation values (null, 0, false, empty string, empty array, empty object): 6/6 now produce a C2X finding. Five produce the typed 'relation must be a JSON string checked against the fact-plane registry ... truthiness never gates the registry lookup'; the empty string, being a genuine JSON string, correctly falls through to the registry lookup and produces "C2X: relation '' is not in the fact-plane registry". Both routes are correct; neither is silent.
Controls held: relation='vibes' still yields the registry finding, and the unmutated valid entry still yields zero findings.

soleOwnershipOfRelation.question: Is _coverage_relation_findings genuinely the SOLE owner of `relation`, so that no overlapping check can mask a regression?
soleOwnershipOfRelation.answer: YES, and it is enforced structurally rather than by convention.
evidence: _validate_coverage's per-field type loop contains an explicit `if fld not in entry or fld == 'relation': continue` — relation is deliberately excluded from the generic field walk.

Only two functions in the module mention 'relation' in a Coverage context: _validate_coverage (2 mentions, both the exclusion) and _coverage_relation_findings (13 mentions, the whole implementation). The third mention site is _s_truthy_relation, which is the retained SOURCE MUTATION that re-breaks the property.

The falsifier is genuine: the retained mutation 'restore the truthiness short-circuit on relation' produces exactly one failure — 'C4 reject-null-relation: expected REJECTION (violates C2X) but the entry validated'. Because ownership is sole, that single mutation is a true falsifier rather than one of two redundant tests masking each other. I confirmed this in the live selftest output.

probe_commitmentsUnmoved.requirement: Verify independently with my OWN from-scratch encoder written from the declared grammar — a stronger test than reusing v3's code.
probe_commitmentsUnmoved.method: I implemented opensip-canonical-json-v1 from the prose in c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json planIntent.canonicalCommitment.encoding alone. My implementation shares NO code with either checker: it does not call json.dumps and does not call _normalise_json. I wrote my own string escaper (NFC, lowercase shortest escapes, solidus unescaped, \u00xx for other control characters), my own integer serialiser (shortest base-10, no leading plus or leading zero), my own key ordering (ascending Unicode scalar value with NFC collision rejection), my own array and container emitters, and my own float refusal. The preimage is UTF8(domain tag) || 0x00 || that encoding, digested with SHA-256 and prefixed 'sha256:'.
probe_commitmentsUnmoved.result: 7 of 7 declared planIntentCommitment vectors reproduce EXACTLY.
probe_commitmentsUnmoved.strongerThanDigestEquality: All 7 PREIMAGES are BYTE-IDENTICAL to those produced by check-c2-v4.py's encoder, not merely digest-equal. A digest collision cannot explain the agreement.
probe_commitmentsUnmoved.unmovedFromV3: All 7 id->digest pairs are IDENTICAL to those declared in the pinned c2-plan-stage-schema.v3.json. Zero commitments moved.
probe_commitmentsUnmoved.thirdIndependentEncoder: The pinned check-c2.py, executed from its hash-verified snapshot, also reproduces 7/7. Three mutually independent encoders agree.
probe_commitmentsUnmoved.negativeControlProvesMyEncoderDiscrimina: My encoder is not vacuously agreeing. Setting schemaVersion to boolean true yields sha256:e86f8120f91c200f5810f9b81393badd2df2fe4478eb74be91e9fe4cc16c1d8b — which is BYTE-FOR-BYTE the second digest the v3 live-bytes review recorded as LB-C2-01's evidence. My independently written encoder therefore corroborates the prior finding's evidence as well as the repair. Setting schemaVersion to 1.0 causes my encoder to REFUSE with 'floating-point numbers are forbidden', matching the declared data model.

areTheWireSurfacesGenuinelyTotalUNGUARDE.falsifiabilityOfTheZeros: The zeros are not decorative. probe_theDeclaredUnguardedGuardedSplit.myAssessmentOfTheARGUMENT: The argument is sound and, more importantly, it is the honest shape. The distinction being drawn is real: a contract document is consumed structurally by _check as an authoring artifact, whereas PlanIntent, Coverage and stage plans are caller-controlled. The three caller-controlled surfaces are total UNGUARDED, which is the strong property, and they are the surfaces all three prior parsed-JSON findings lived on. Publishing 2517 as a measured, named, in-band number — instead of wrapping _check in a broader try/except to manufacture a zero — is the behaviour this corpus has repeatedly failed to produce. I specifically checked that the number is not being hidden: it appears in the selftest banner, in RES-C2V4-05 and in contractRoot.unguardedEscapesRule.
probe_theDeclaredUnguardedGuardedSplit.residualIRecordAgainstIt: unguardedEscapes at the contract root is REPORTED but not PINNED, so a future edit that raises it from 2517 to 25170 would print a different number and still exit 0. The candidate's own stated reason — that pinning a count of a document's own mutations inside that document has no fixed point — is correct, and no better mechanism is obvious. Recorded as RES-IR-03, not as a finding.

findings.class: Identical class to EV10-IR-01 in check-evidence-v10.py
findings.title: integer_guard_scan's reachability, taint, function-universe, numeric-literal and operator models are each narrower than the property it advertises, so a genuine LB-C2-01 defect can be reintroduced behind eleven different indirections while the scan publishes zero unguarded sites
declaredClaimViolated: check-c2-v4.py module docstring: 'a scan of this checker's own syntax tree that refuses any bare numeric comparison against a wire-sourced value anywhere in the reachable validator closure, so a fifth site cannot be added silently'

Section 1 comment: 'Nothing else in the reachable validator closure may compare a wire-sourced value to a numeric literal, and _integer_guard_scan enforces that over this file's own abstract syntax tree on every run'

c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json planIntent.integerConstantFields.rule: 'check-c2-v4.py additionally scans its own abstract syntax tree and refuses to report clean if any reachable validator compares a wire-sourced value to a numeric literal outside the declared guard helpers'
findings.rootCause: Five independent narrowings compose. (1) _module_functions considers only ast.FunctionDef in tree.body, so class methods, module-level lambdas, async defs and nested defs are outside the universe entirely. (2) _reachable follows only ast.Call whose .func is an ast.Name in that universe — the exact EV10-IR-01 shape — so aliases, getattr dispatch, dispatch tables and callbacks are invisible. (3) _tainted_names propagates only through single-target ast.Assign from a Subscript/.get()/tainted Name, so walrus, tuple unpack, AnnAssign, for-targets and comprehension targets all launder taint away. (4) _numeric_literal accepts only a bare ast.Constant, so comparison against a module-level named constant is invisible. (5) In/NotIn are skipped outright, although `True in {1}` is True and is the same defect.

evidence.constructive: 13-variant battery. 11 variants restored the FULL live LB-C2-01 defect — validate_plan_intent returning zero findings for schemaVersion true AND 1.0 — while the author's own integer_guard_scan reported unguardedNumericComparisons = 0. Only the direct inline form and a directly-Name-called renamed helper were reported.
evidence.notHypothetical: The blind spot already covers shipped code: _is_relative_path (line 472) is a genuine caller-supplied-data validator whose only reference is the callback `validator=_is_relative_path` at line 713. It is absent from the author's reached set of 69 and present in my reached set of 77. It happens to be written correctly, so there is no exposure today.
evidence.scanIsNotVacuous: guardHelperCallSites = 30 on the frozen bytes and a floor of 8 is enforced, so the scan is genuinely non-vacuous for the cases it does model.

whyNotBlocking: NO FALSE ACCEPT IS REACHABLE ON THE FROZEN BYTES, established by enumeration rather than assumption: zero non-Name/non-Attribute call sites in 1548 calls; zero getattr/eval/exec function dispatch; zero decorators; zero top-level async defs; the only 6 classes are infrastructure with 7 non-validating methods; the only 3 dispatch tables hold mutation authors, not validators.
MY OWN SCAN, widened on all five axes simultaneously, finds ZERO unguarded sites on the frozen bytes.

AN EXHAUSTIVE SWEEP INDEPENDENT OF ANY REACHABILITY MODEL finds exactly seven numeric-literal comparisons in the whole 3238-line module, and all seven compare Python-internal integers — len(), list lengths, loop counters — never wire data.

THE BEHAVIOURAL LAYER IS AN INDEPENDENT, NON-AST BACKSTOP that caught 13 of 13 evasion variants with a named LB-C2-01 finding and exit 1. It cannot be evaded syntactically because it injects values and observes admissions. Defence in depth genuinely holds here — this is not the check-evidence-v10 situation where the scan was the only guard.
findings.reproducibleCondition: In a disposable copy of artifacts/, replace the single line `    if not _schema_version_ok(intent.get("schemaVersion")):` in _validate_plan_intent with `    if (sv := intent.get("schemaVersion")) != 1:` and change nothing else. Call integer_guard_scan(ast.parse(source)): unguardedNumericComparisons == 0. Call validate_plan_intent with schemaVersion=True: returns []. Fully deterministic; 13/13 variants reproduced on every attempt.
findings.requiredRepair: Do not weaken the behavioural layer, which is what actually holds the line. Strengthen the scan so its advertised scope matches its delivered scope, by either (a) narrowing the CLAIM — restate the docstring, the Section 1 comment and integerConstantFields.rule as 'refuses a bare numeric comparison in any top-level function reachable by direct name call', which is exactly what is delivered — or (b) widening the SCAN: collect every FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/Lambda at any depth including class bodies; treat a bare Name reference to a module function as a reachability edge so callbacks like _is_relative_path are covered; propagate taint through NamedExpr, AnnAssign, AugAssign, tuple/list unpack, for-targets and comprehension targets; treat a module-level name bound to a numeric constant as a numeric literal; and stop skipping In/NotIn against containers holding numeric literals. Option (b) is preferable and I confirmed it costs nothing on these bytes — my widened scan still reports zero, so adopting it would not manufacture false findings. Whichever is chosen, add retained SCAN_MUTATIONS for at least the alias, callback, walrus, named-constant and membership shapes, so the widened property is itself falsifiable.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: If any of the eleven evading variants had produced a green run, or if my widened scan or exhaustive sweep had found even one unguarded wire comparison in the frozen bytes, this would be BLOCKING. Neither occurred.

verdictStatement.basis: Both blocking findings are genuinely repaired, verified by probes I wrote rather than by replaying the author's fixtures. All seven planIntentCommitment vectors reproduce byte-exactly under a from-scratch encoder I implemented from the declared grammar alone, sharing no code with either checker, with byte-identical preimages and a negative control that independently reproduces the prior review's own LB-C2-01 evidence digest. My independent enumeration reproduces every published totality count exactly on all four surfaces, reconciling to the declared pathsNotRoundTripping with zero silent path collisions. All 123 silent accepts are located individually and all 123 are genuinely declared-open for the surface that produced them, including the 84 at the stage-plan surface whose declared scope split I falsified by driving the binding surface and finding 24 of 24 hostile identity values rejected. The declared unguarded/guarded split is honest, declared in three places before the fact, and its load-bearing half — that the three caller-controlled wire surfaces are total UNGUARDED — is true and falsifiable. The selftest genuinely executes, proven by neutralising a mutation to a no-op and observing ESCAPE / SELFTEST-FAIL / exit 1. Hash-before-execution holds under runtime instrumentation with exactly one read per pinned input, no check/read gap, and sys.modules poisoning defeated. All four declared frozen inputs are byte-identical at start and end and both predecessors are preserved. The one new finding is real and is of the same class an independent reviewer just used to reject check-evidence-v10, but I established by AST-level reference enumeration, by a scan widened on five axes, and by an exhaustive whole-module sweep that its blind spot is currently empty, and by a 13-variant constructive battery that an independent non-AST behavioural layer catches every evasion. No false accept is reachable on these bytes.
